mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that compresses equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This effect is consistently observed during rate-cut cycles across historical data.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0% and remains elevated for three consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates broad-based consumer demand weakness that triggers equity sell-offs as corporate revenue growth prospects deteriorate, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS decline > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 0.5% in 1 month, or Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% year-over-year), a rising federal funds rate signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates and reduces risk appetite, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS rises, or Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production exceeding 1.0% over three consecutive months signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate profits and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO declines > 1.0% in 3 months, or Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained expansion in real GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates robust economic conditions that support corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days. This relationship holds consistently during economic expansions.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth is positive, or Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and unemployment rate signals dual monetary tightening and labor market weakness that severely dampens economic activity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE rises, or Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market slowdown regime (HOUST < 1200.0 thousand units), a concurrent decline in retail sales (RSAFS) signals severe consumer demand contraction that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1200.0 and RSAFS declines, or Rank IC is below 0.03.
